label: Bing Chat
summary: Bing Chat is an LLM-based conversational interface built by Microsoft, designed with chat affordances like text bubbles and a 'Chat' button. It became a case study in the gap between what designers intended (search) and what users actually did (open-ended conversation and social interaction). Maaike uses it as an example of a system that lacks real conversational grounding and risks encouraging anthropomorphism.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike uses Bing Chat as a concrete, somewhat absurd illustration of what goes wrong when you deploy an LLM in a conversational interface without understanding what conversation actually is. Drawing on Enfield's work on dialogue, she argues that Bing Chat can mirror conversational form but cannot participate in the collaborative, intention-tracking, morally-grounded process that real conversation requires. Microsoft's surprise at user behaviour is, for her, a symptom of not doing basic conversation 101: if you design a chatty persona with chat affordances, people will treat it as a conversational partner, and the system will not be able to hold up its end of that bargain.
open_questions: Will it ever be possible for a machine to form the same kind of interlocking conversational system with a human that two humans form with each other?
The post is cut off before finishing the comparison between Bing Chat and ChatGPT — what distinction was Maaike drawing there?
